findings.function: all functions that read the Well's immutable data (tokens, wellFunction, pumps, reserves...)
findings.source: Clone._getImmutableArgsOffset / _getArgUint256 / ClonePlus._getArgIERC20Array: offset := sub(calldatasize(), shr(240, calldataload(sub(calldatasize(), 2))))
findings.issue: The immutable-args offset, a pure function of calldata, is re-expanded inside every calldata index, and the number of tokens `cd[off + 20]` inside every memory address; this one subexpression is on 2,056 of the 9,465 lines and makes most lines several hundred characters long.
findings.rule: Calldata never changes during a call, so a calldata-only expression used many times can be bound once to a named variable at the function entry (common-subexpression elimination over pure, state-independent expressions).

findings.function: shift(address,uint256,address) and every function using _getJ (15 copies)
findings.decompiled: if 0 >= mem[128]: mem[mem[64]] = 0x672215de...; revert with memory from mem[64] len _502 - mem[64] + 4 ; _506 = mem[160]; s = 0; while -address(_506) + _param1: if s + 1 >= mem[128]: revert ... ; _506 = mem[32 * s + 192]; s = s + 1
findings.source: Well.sol:843-848 for (j; j < _tokens.length; ++j) { if (jToken == _tokens[j]) return j; } revert InvalidTokens();
findings.issue: The search loop is rotated (first test and element before the loop, P3), its condition `-address(_506) + _param1` is a disguised `_param1 != _tokens[s]`, and the InvalidTokens() revert is raw memory with length `_502 - mem[64] + 4` although `_502` was just copied from mem[64] (= 4).
findings.rule: Print a difference used as a truth value as `a != b`; un-rotate loops whose pre-header duplicates the body's first test; fold `x - mem[64]` to 0 when x is a copy of mem[64] with no store to slot 64 in between, which then lets the revert be decoded as `InvalidTokens()`.

findings.function: getAddLiquidityOut(uint256[]) and the other view/write paths ending with a well-function call
findings.decompiled: static call cd[off + 52] >> 96 with: args mem[mem[64] len _52 + 32 * _53 + ceil32(_56) - mem[64] + 132] ... mem[64] = ceil32(return_data.size) + mem[64]; mem[_58 + ceil32(return_data.size)] = SafeMath.sub(mem[_58], totalSupply); return memory from mem[64] len _58 + ceil32(return_data.size) - mem[64] + 32
findings.issue: The calcLpTokenSupply(uint256[],bytes) call (0x14c15fc0) loses its name and arguments (P2), and the return is raw memory although mem[64] was just set to `_58 + ceil32(return_data.size)`, so the returned value is simply `SafeMath.sub(ext_call.return_data[0], totalSupply)`. 29 `return memory` and many `revert with memory` lines share this cause.
findings.rule: Track the value just stored to mem[64] and substitute it into later reads of mem[64] (until the next store), then fold `a - a`; apply it to return/revert/log ranges as well as call arguments.

findings.function: pumps() and every function that builds Call[] (22 copies)
findings.issue: The compiler's per-element allocation of a struct array is printed as a rotated count-down loop (first element before the loop, `while idx - 1`), an obscure form of an implicit loop (P3).
findings.rule: Un-rotate a loop whose pre-header repeats one body iteration, giving `idx = 0; while idx < N:`; a loop that only allocates zeroed structs and stores their pointers could print as one `new struct[N]` line.

findings.source: EIP712Upgradeable._EIP712Version(): copy of the long `_version` string
findings.issue: Under the dominating `_18 > 31`, the length `-c + max(c + 224, _18 + c + 192) - 193` is just `_18 - 1`, as in the first string's copy (`floor32(_2 - 1)`), but it is printed unsimplified.
findings.rule: Simplify `max(a + x, a + y)` to `a + max(x, y)`, then use the dominating range of `y` to resolve the max.

notes: Functions over ~700 lines (the swap, add/remove liquidity, shift, sync families: 2406-9465) reviewed by structure (loops, calls, storage writes, events, reverts); the others fully. Source loops, all shown as while: getAddLiquidityOut/getRemoveLiquidityImbalancedIn/getShiftOut/getSyncOut/removeLiquidity/removeLiquidityImbalanced/shift/skim/sync token loops, init's nested duplicate check (`while True` with the epilogue in the exit branch + inner `while idx < N`), pumps() loop, LibBytes.readUint128 (`while idx <= N` with an unfolded `idx - 1 > idx` check, 18 copies), LibBytes.storeUint128 (`while s < mem[_518] / 2`), _addLiquidity x2, _getIJ (`while True` with breaks), _getJ (rotated, see finding), _setReserves, _updatePumps, _authorizeUpgrade. Implicit loops: 74 uint256[]/address[] memory-to-memory ABI encodings (P7), 22 struct-array allocations (P3), 2 address[] decodes with validation. Zero-fill copies from `call.data[calldata.size len ...]` immediately overwritten by the real copy (P8, 121 lines). Storage strings (init's name/symbol/EIP712 name and version) are shown as copy lines, correctly; the short version string '1' is written as three field writes (`uint8(stor104) = 2; uint240(stor104.field_8) = 0; stor104.field_248 = 49`, P15). Custom errors and events of the Well are mostly unnamed (database), e.g. `revert with Bytes(16, 0x213509ed...), mem[... len 20]` for DuplicateTokens(address), and 9 `log 0x...` with raw-memory data. No semantic error found.
summary: Faithful and complete text (no aborts, all 21 source loops as whiles), but very hard to read: the Clone immutable-args offset is re-expanded on 2,056 lines, the free-memory pointer is not resolved for calls, returns and reverts, and implicit ABI/allocation loops appear as 98 obscure whiles.
